title: Stop the Car, and the Guide Tells You More | vitalii.no
description:
Every place on a road-trip guide only ever got one short story, built from a small slice of its local-history article. Stop the car — park by a farm, walk around a church — and the app had nothing left to say beyond what was already heard driving past.

Android now watches for exactly that moment: a dwell below 15 km/h right after the first story finishes. When it happens, the runner pulls the full lokalhistoriewiki article instead of the short excerpt used for the first pass, plus every other local-history page that mentions the same place, and writes a second, deeper story that explicitly skips anything already told.

The source behind the first story was a short excerpt; the deep version now reads up to 12,000 characters from the main article alone, growing past 32,000 characters once related pages are folded in. A database migration tracks deep-story status per place so anywhere you actually stop jumps the queue ahead of the daily pre-written batch.
